elements.requirement: Where a magistrates’ court has power to issue a warrant of control under this Part of this Act, the court may postpone the issue of the warrant until such time and on such conditions, if any, as it thinks just, provided the court thinks it expedient to do so.
elements.quote: postpone the issue of the warrant until such time and on such conditions, if any, as the court thinks just

elements.requirement: Where a magistrates’ court has power to issue a warrant of commitment under this Part of this Act, the court may, if it thinks it expedient to do so, fix a term of imprisonment or detention under section 108 of the Powers of Criminal Courts (Sentencing) Act 2000 and postpone the issue of the warrant until such time and on such conditions, if any, as it thinks just.
elements.quote: fix a term of imprisonment or detention under section 108 of the powers of Criminal Courts (Sentencing) Act 2000 (detention of persons aged 18 to 20 for default)and postpone the issue of the warrant

elements.requirement: A magistrates’ court has the power at any time to direct that the issue of a warrant of commitment be postponed until a time different from that previously set, or to vary any postponement conditions, or both, but only if the court thinks it just to do so having regard to a change of circumstances since the relevant time.
elements.quote: to vary any of the conditions on which its issue is postponed, but only if it thinks it just to do so having regard to a change of circumstances since the relevant time

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 77, where neither of the powers conferred by subsection (3) has been exercised previously, the relevant time is defined as the date when the issue of the warrant was postponed under subsection (2).
elements.quote: the date when the issue of the warrant was postponed under subsection (2) above

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 77, in any case where either or both powers conferred by subsection (3) have been exercised previously, the relevant time is defined as the date of the exercise or latest exercise of either or both of those powers.
elements.quote: the date of the exercise or latest exercise of either or both of the powers

elements.requirement: A justice of the peace acting in the local justice area in which a warrant has been or would have been issued must refer an application to the court if, on application by a person in respect of whom issue of the warrant was postponed, it appears to the justice that since the relevant time there has been a change of circumstances making it just for the court to exercise one or both powers under subsection (3).
elements.quote: he shall refer the application to the court

elements.requirement: Where an application is referred to the court under subsection (5), the court must fix a time and place for the hearing of the application.
elements.quote: the ... court shall fix a time and place for the application to be heard

elements.requirement: Where an application is referred to the court under subsection (5), the designated officer for the court must give the applicant notice of the time and place fixed for the hearing.
elements.quote: the designated officer for the court shall give the applicant notice of that time and place

elements.requirement: The court may proceed with the consideration of the application in the applicant's absence if notice of the hearing has been given but the applicant fails to appear at the specified time and place.
elements.quote: the court may proceed with the consideration of the application in his absence

elements.requirement: If a warrant of commitment in respect of the sum adjudged to be paid was issued before the hearing of the application, the court has the power to order that the warrant cease to have effect and, if the applicant was arrested under it, to order the applicant's release.
elements.quote: the court shall have power to order that the warrant shall cease to have effect and, if the applicant has been arrested in pursuance of it, to order that he shall be released

elements.requirement: The court may only order that a warrant of commitment cease to have effect or that the applicant be released if it is satisfied that the change of circumstances relied upon by the applicant was not put before the court when it determined whether to issue the warrant.
elements.quote: only make an order under this subsection if it is satisfied that the change of circumstances on which the applicant relies was not put before the court when it was determining whether to issue the warrant
